text.title: C4 Drift Detection from IaC Decision Tree

decision-tree.root-question: Is there both a machine-readable C4 model (Structurizr DSL/JSON, LikeC4, or model YAML with stable ids) and applied IaC state (Terraform state, Pulumi stack, CloudFormation stack) for the same system?

branch.conclusion: Skip. With no applied state there is nothing live to compare against; hand-managed infrastructure needs an inventory source first.
Transcribe the diagram into a model with stable element ids and render pictures from it; re-enter the tree once the model is committed.

branch.question: Does the comparison read applied state (`terraform show -json`, `pulumi stack export`, `DescribeStackResources`) and record the state serial or export version plus the model commit hash in the report?

branch.conclusion: Repoint the comparison from source files to state output and stamp both identities on the report.

branch.question: Are the resource-to-element mapping table and the noise allowlist version-controlled, with `unmapped` and suppressed counts printed so the totals reconcile?

branch.conclusion: Commit the mapping table, emit an `unmapped` section with counts, and reconcile state resource totals in the report header.
Move every suppression from code into the allowlist file and print the suppressed count per entry.
Run the full procedure: three drift classes with ids, stated comparison level, post-apply plus scheduled runs, closure by commit or expiry; emit the drift report per the output contract.

example.p: Structurizr DSL model in `docs/c4/` and a Terraform state for `orders-prod` both exist. The current script parses `.tf` files → conclusion r-compare-applied-state-not-source. After switching to `terraform show -json`, the mapping table is committed but `continue` skips for `aws_iam_role` live in the script → r-noise-allowlist-explicit on the next pass.
